sourceInformation.genre: Action adventure with exploration, inventory puzzles and cooperative play
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPU with engine WebGL2 fallback, Rapier 3D 0.19.3, Web Audio API, Gamepad API, AI Hub Session Protocol v1 / client 1.4.0, PeerJS 1.5.5
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded desert dioramas with ink edges, warm sandstone, teal shadows and pulp expedition typography
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip: breathing, running, whipping, dodging and flute playing; procedural environmental motion
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized expedition score, procedural sound effects and Animalese-style gibberish voices; music defaults to 10 percent
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 shared-world cooperative play through AI Hub; standalone WebRTC room codes and same-browser BroadcastChannel; local second-controller co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium 153 with software WebGPU; complete scripted expedition at default balance; simulated standard gamepad and touch; direct file URL deployment; two-page co-op; official AI Hub standard, dedicated-server, host-leave and 150 ms latency / 50 ms jitter / 5 percent loss scenarios; offline synthesized audio. Physical controller, real mobile hardware and listening quality unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Atari 1982 instruction manual: rooms, inventory, enemies, whip, flute, shovel, parachute, sun-map and mesa mechanics; Raiders2600 reverse-engineering notes on abstract room rendering and two-channel TIA music/effects; AI Hub integration documentation; official Three.js and Rapier documentation.

testingFeedback: Testing caught five distinct issues: missing AI Hub metadata, an obscured east dial, overlapping dial labels, an exit lintel obscuring the explorer, and shader-loading time incorrectly counting toward title inactivity. All were corrected; review also corrected gameplay and control defects.
One testing issue blocked AI Hub acceptance. Review additionally found two progression blockers: unrecoverable stolen coins and touch controls unable to break supply crates; both were fixed.
The scripted four-chapter playthrough and official AI Hub harness were most useful for checking progression and network lifecycle behavior.
Syntax-only checking was least useful because it could not assess progression, input focus or visual visibility.
engineFeedback: Three.js made custom modeled dioramas, toon shading and native character animation straightforward.
Collider origin conventions, menu focus and guest snapshot handling needed corrections. Headless WebGPU screenshots were blank; state checks and the engine WebGL fallback supported verification.
The complete adventure layer: inventory puzzles, interaction, camera, controls, co-op replication and procedural audio.
Coordinating asynchronous WebGPU startup, Rapier collision movement and authoritative network state.
A smaller first-party controller and physics integration layer would simplify polished game creation.
promptFeedback: The source-first research, TV-friendly controller design and complete expedition scope gave the game a clear identity.
The source year identifies the Atari game rather than the 1981 film; that distinction needed research.
Integrating a complete four-chapter adventure with standalone and hosted co-op in one HTML file.
Specify an approximate target playtime and whether online play should include public matchmaking or private room codes.

aiHub.name: Raiders of the Lost Hieroglyph
aiHub.description: Crack open a desert mystery in a cel-shaded pulp expedition. Trade for tools, decode the sun map, whip across a canyon and charm the vault's snakes before a very large boulder interrupts your research.
aiHub.controls: WASD/arrows move, mouse aim/click whip, E interact, Space dodge, Q flute, Tab notes, Esc pause; standard gamepad supported; touch drag movement with assisted combat.
